title: How Long an AI UGC Ad Takes to Make, From Brief to Live Ad
summary: An AI UGC ad renders quickly, but scripts, retakes, review and Meta's learning phase set the real timeline. See published turnarounds and what slows them down.
body_markdown:
## How real creator timelines compare


The creator packages in our library publish longer timelines. Brighter Click's[UGC agency page](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) gives 10 to 14 business days for its 12-video package. The UGC Agency's[homepage](https://theugc.agency/) describes a 21-day target for its first round of finished ads, with each stage approved before the next. That is slower than a managed AI batch, but it is the route to use when a real customer has to appear on camera.


## A sample schedule from brief to read-out


This is an illustration built from the published figures above, not a measured result. Say you want to judge a first batch of AI UGC ads about two weeks after you brief them.


- **Day 0.** Send the brief with one claim you can prove, the offer, the presenter preference and the formats.
- **Days 1 to 5.** Script approval, then production. A provider with a day-five first batch delivers at the end of this window; a provider with a week-one promise delivers a day or two later.
- **Days 6 and 7.** Review the batch against the approved claims. Plan one retake round for the ads that miss.
- **Day 8.** Launch the approved ads and stop editing the ad set.
- **Day 15.** Read the results. Meta says an ad set usually leaves learning after about 50 results in the week after its last significant edit, so a read on day nine tells you about delivery, not the creative.


Work backward from the date you need the read-out, then add a day of slack for the first draft to fail review. Put the read-out on the calendar at launch, and hold edits until it passes unless an ad breaks a rule.


## What makes an AI UGC ad take longer than it should


- **Script changes after approval.** A changed line in an AI presenter ad means a re-render, and a re-render means new credits on a self-serve tool and another review. Lock the claims before the first render.
- **Formats and languages.** Each aspect ratio, caption version and translation is another output to check. Four aspect ratios with captions and hooks, as 351 Studio lists in its deliverables, is a useful checklist for your own spec.
- **Revision rounds.** Set the number before the work starts. An open-ended process can run past the published turnaround, because the quote covers a set number of rounds.
- **Claim review.** Keep a list of claims that need proof before render. If the ad presents a customer's experience, it needs a real customer, not an avatar.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify, our top pick, delivers its first batch on day five and makes about 25 finished ads a week, with a person checking each one.
- Published managed timelines range from 48 hours at Creatify Studio to a two-week first batch at Adguns, so confirm when each clock starts.
- Self-serve renders are quick, but every script change re-renders the presenter and uses credits.
- Plan for about a week of Meta learning after launch before you judge the ads.
- Real creator ads take longer, but they are the only route here that puts a real customer on camera.


## FAQ


### How long does it take to make an AI UGC ad from start to finish?


A managed provider can deliver a first batch in days. Knowlify's first batch lands on day five, and Vidful says its first creatives arrive by the end of week one. Self-serve tools render in a session, but your scripting and review set the real finish date, and Meta's learning phase adds about a week before you can judge the ad.


### Can a provider deliver an AI UGC ad in one week?


Some publish that pace or faster. Knowlify's first batch lands on day five, Unreal UGC lists a 3 to 5 day turnaround, Vidful says first creatives arrive by the end of week one, and Creatify's pricing page lists a 48-hour turnaround for Studio. Check whether the clock starts at kickoff, at approval or at the first draft, and confirm how many revision rounds are included.


### Why does an AI UGC ad take longer after the first render?


Each change to the script, the presenter or the voice can require a new render. HeyGen's avatar guidance says A-roll changes need re-rendering and consume credits, so check the speech and scenes before rendering.


### When can I judge an AI ad's results?


Not in the first two days. Meta says an ad set usually leaves its learning phase after about 50 results in the week after its last significant edit, so keep edits to a minimum while the ad learns.


### How long does a real creator ad take?


Brighter Click gives 10 to 14 business days for its 12-video package, and The UGC Agency targets 21 days for its first round of finished ads. Creator ads take longer because casting, filming and approval involve a real person, and that is also why they remain the choice for a real customer's story.
